newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania coffee industry worries over new taxes.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania coffee industry worries over new taxes.

text.p: Hit by declining output, senior coffee industry officials said they were concerned about a government proposal to impose Value Added Tax (VAT) on coffee exports.

"The (Tanzania Coffee) Association is definitely worried about this tax system and is praying the government reviews the act and should do so very fast," said one trader, who declined to be identified.
Jeremy Lefroy, Moshi-based Managing Director of the American Coffee Company, said on Wednesday at an annual coffee conference of widespread bankruptcies if the government put VAT on exports.
Under a fiscal reform programme, the government is set to introduce VAT next year. It would apply to all exports.
A 10-20 percent VAT on coffee exports would be disastrous to the Tanzanian coffee industry, said Lefroy, who recommended that the industry lobby the treasury for a waiver for coffee.

The TCA, inaugurated last Wednesday, is the sole private body representing Tanzania's coffee industry. It originated from the now-defunct Tanzania Coffee Traders Association, a body which represented mostly exporters.
